newsitem.title: USA: IMF WILL KNOW IN '97 IF GOLD MUST BE SOLD - OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: IMF WILL KNOW IN '97 IF GOLD MUST BE SOLD - OFFICIAL.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund should know sometime next year whether it will need to sell gold to finance stepped-up aid to poor nations, IMF Interim Committee Chairman Philippe Maystadt said on Tuesday.

He suggested in an interview with Reuters that Germany would go along with the sale should bilateral contributions from IMF member nations fall short of what is needed to finance the increased assistance.
"There is an understanding agreed upon," Maystadt said. "If the need arises we must all be prepared to optimise the use of the Fund's reserves."

Germany publicly has consistently opposed the sale of IMF gold to finance a continuation of the Fund's Enhanced Structural Adjustment (lending) Facility and its participation in a mutilateral debt relief initiative for poor nations.

But Maystadt, who is also Belgian Finance Minister, said that German representatives at the IMF board and the Interim Committee have agreed that the Fund must be prepared to optimize its reserves -- code for gold sales -- if need be.

"It is true that until now the German representatives have never given their agreement to the sale of gold," he said. "But it is true also that the German representatives agreed in the Executive Board and later in the Interim Committee on the understandings (about optimizing IMF reserves)."
He said the IMF should know "in the course of next year" whether gold will need to be sold.
Despite the uncertainty surrounding gold sales, the IMF, the World bank and the Paris Club of creditor countries decided this week to launch their jont debt relief programs for poor countries.

Maystadt said that anywhere from 13 to 20 countries could benefit from the plan. He declined to say which nation might be first, saying that depended on negotiations between the IMF, the World Bank and the Paris Club.
"I hope before the end of the year one or two countries' cases might be taken up," he said.
